prose:
OpenRouter's 22 November announcement describes its response to researchers' findings that some inference providers failed to uphold data policies or had data compromised. The company says it off-boarded three providers, removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility, including precautionary removals, and notified potentially affected customers. It lists statements from Novita, Phala and Together, while noting that not all affected providers have posted publicly. It says work continues on recurring checks, verification of forwarding paths and validation before removed endpoints can regain ZDR eligibility.

This is the routing layer's own account of its response to the Dragos canary investigation already covered from Dragos and Ars Technica, not a new independent experiment. OpenRouter says the findings did not show a breach or unauthorized access of OpenRouter itself. Exposure through an inference provider and compromise of the router's systems are different claims. The reported removals, notifications and safeguards were not independently audited here; precautionary removal also does not establish that every affected endpoint leaked data.
highlights: OpenRouter reports three inference providers off-boarded
Company says 125 endpoints lost ZDR eligibility, including precautionary removals
The announcement says potentially affected customers were notified
Provider statements from Novita, Phala and Together are listed
Not all affected providers have published their own accounts
Forwarding-path checks and validation before restoring ZDR eligibility are described
OpenRouter says the findings showed no breach of its own systems
Company response to the same Dragos investigation, not an independent audit
